October 23, 2026
Dear Sir/ Madam,
Sub: Outcome of the Board meeting
This has reference to our letter dated September 15, 2026, regarding the captioned subject. The Board, at
their meeting held on October 22-23, 2026 transacted the following items of business:
Financial Results:
1. Approved the audited consolidated financial results of the Company and its subsidiaries as per
Indian Accounting Standards (“INDAS”) for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;
2. Approved the audited standalone financial results of the Company as per INDAS for the quarter
and half year ended September 30, 2026;
3. Approved the audited financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries as per INDAS and
International Financial Reporting Standard (“IFRS”) for the quarter and half year ended September
30, 2026;
Dividend:
4. Declared an interim dividend of ₹ 26/- per equity share, fixed November 3, 2026 as a record date
and November 11, 2026 as a payout date.
Stock grants:
5. Based on the recommendations of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board
approved the grant of 9,640 Restricted Stock Units (‘RSUs’) under the 2015 Incentive
Compensation Plan (’2015 Plan’) to eligible employees. The grants made under the 2015 Plan
would vest equally over a period of three years. The RSUs will be granted w.e.f., November 1, 2026
and the exercise price will be equal to the par value of the share.

Allotment of equity shares:
6. Allotted 15,578 equity shares of face value of ₹ 5/- each, pursuant to exercise of Restricted Stock
Units by eligible employees as hereunder:
• 2,841 equity shares under the 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan;
• 12,737 equity shares under the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019.
Consequently, effective from October 23, 2026, the issued and subscribed share capital of the
Company stands increased to ₹ 20,29,14,60,780/- divided into 4,05,82,92,156 equity shares of ₹5/-
each.
The Board meeting was held on October 22 and 23, 2026. The Board meeting on October 23,
2026 commenced at 12.27 PM IST and concluded at 4.00 PM IST.
We are hereby enclosing herewith the financial results, press releases, and other annexures mentioned
above. The same will also be made available on the Company’s website www.infosys.com.
This is for your information and records.
Yours sincerely,

We have audited the accompanying statement of Consolidated Financial Results of INFOSYS LIMITED
(the "Company") and its subsidiaries (the Company and its subsidiaries together referred to as the

by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (the "LODR Regulations").
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, the
Statement:
(i) includes the financial results of the subsidiaries as given in the Annexure to this report;
(ii) is presented in accordance with the requirements of Regulation 33 of the LODR Regulations; and
(iii) gives a true and fair view in conformity with the recognition and measurement principles laid down
in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial Reporting" (''Ind AS 34") prescribed under
section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 (the "Act") read with relevant rules issued thereunder

consolidated other comprehensive income and other financial information of the Group for the

We conducted our audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing ("SA"s) specified under Section

consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 under the

evidence obtained by us is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion.

Bengaluru, India – October 23, 2026: Infosys (NSE, BSE, NYSE: INFY), a global leader in AI-first
business consulting and technology services, delivered $5,145 million in Q2 revenues, year on year
growth of 1.5% and sequential growth of 1.2% in constant currency. Operating margin was stable at
21.0%. EPS growth was 8.7% year on year in rupee terms. TCV of large deal wins was $5.2 billion, with
62% net new.
H1 revenues grew at 1.9% year on year in constant currency. Operating margin for H1 was at 21.0%.
“We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our
position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex
transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5% and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter. As
enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our
differentiated market positioning and client confidence,” said Salil Parekh, CEO and MD. “We are
advising some of the largest global enterprise on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain
and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock
AI value at scale,” he added.

Client Wins & Testimonials
• Infosys collaborated with Mondelez International to drive its supply chain transformation through
AI-enabled decision-making, data standardization, and intelligent enterprise workflows. Sanjay
Gurbaxani, Global Vice President, Digital Supply Chain, Mondelez International, said,
“From digitally connected supply chain to standardizing data and enabling more informed
decision-making, the opportunity lies in bringing together people, processes, data, and
technology to deliver meaningful business outcomes. As AI evolves towards agentic AI, the
potential extends beyond generating insights to enable more autonomous, responsive, and
intelligent workflows. The real value comes from embedding intelligence into everyday business
decisions, rethinking established processes, and scaling solutions across the enterprise. With
Infosys we are building a compelling solution where technology, aligned with business priorities,
can become a catalyst for operational excellence and long-term impact.”
• Infosys entered a ten-year strategic agreement with Crocs, Inc. to accelerate its IT
transformation and support scalable global growth. Tom Britt, Chief Information Officer,
Crocs, Inc. said, "As our organization reimagines its IT landscape, we sought a collaborator
who could combine deep domain expertise with a commitment to innovation and operational
excellence. By leveraging Infosys’ proven delivery frameworks and advanced automation
capabilities, we will optimize operations, reduce costs and scale responsibly—while driving
continuous improvement and building a foundation for sustainable growth and digital resilience
that positions Crocs, Inc. for the future."
• Infosys collaborated with Knorr-Bremse to accelerate its AI-enabled enterprise transformation.
Satheeskaran Navaratnam, Chief Digital Officer & VP Transformation & Governance IT,
Knorr-Bremse, said, “At Knorr-Bremse, we are building a future-ready technology foundation
that supports innovation and long-term value creation. Our Tech4Value program is central to
this journey, helping us create a more agile, efficient, and scalable IT environment across the
organization. By working with Infosys, we aim to make our technology estate as optimized and
reliable as the systems we build for our customers, ensuring that every layer of our infrastructure
is equipped to support the pace of change our business demands.”
• Infosys expanded collaboration with Metsä Group to drive AI-led transformation of its IT
landscape. Kristiina Lammila, Chief Information Officer of Metsä Group, said, “This
engagement marks a new chapter in Metsä's long-standing collaboration with Infosys, as we
simplify and transform our IT sourcing model to meet the efficiency demands of today's business
environment. We are confident in our joint ability to deliver on these targets and accelerate the
transformation of Metsä's IT, powered by AI.”
• Infosys collaborated with NTN Corporation to drive its digital growth with seamless SAP cloud
adoption. Kenji Kitazato, Head - ICT Strategy Department, NTN Corporation, said, “This
migration to SAP Commerce Cloud powered by Infosys has streamlined our IT operations,
improved agility, and laid a strong foundation for future digital growth. This transformation
enables us to utilize this new foundation and further promote the use of digital technology.”
• Infosys collaborated with Telia to drive AI-powered transformation across its network and
cybersecurity operations. Hein Müskens, Group CIO, Telia, said, "Infosys' proven expertise in
AI, automation, and telecom transformation made them the ideal partner for this initiative.
Leveraging Infosys Topaz and deep industry knowledge, we look forward to accelerating the
modernization of our network and cybersecurity operations, enhancing efficiency and agility,
and strengthening our foundation for future innovation."
• Infosys collaborated with KnitWell Group to develop an AI-powered platform for its customer
engagement. Jaap van Riel, CTO, KnitWell Group, said, “Our relationship with our customers

information (hereinafter referred to as the "Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements").
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, the
aforesaid Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements give a true and fair view in conformity
with International Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial Reporting" ("IAS 34") as issued by the
International Accounting Standards Board ("IASB"), of the consolidated state of affairs of the Group
as at September 30, 2026, its consolidated profit and its consolidated other comprehensive income

opinion on the Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.

Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the Interim Condensed Consolidated

material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the

As part of an audit in accordance with SAs, we exercise professional judgment and maintain
professional scepticism throughout the audit. We also:

Financial Statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform audit procedures
responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a
basis for our opinion. The risk of not detecting a material misstatement resulting from fraud is
higher than for one resulting from error, as fraud may involve collusion, forgery, intentional
